intent: superclaude — and any other entry point — starts the ground loop if and only if one is not already running, deciding by READING the liveness record, never by scanning for a process.
why: Akien named superclaude as ONE OF the entry points, so the guard cannot live in superclaude: it is a shared door and belongs with the thing it protects (Law 6). Otherwise every future entry point re-derives it, which is Law 1's defect.
falsifier: Two entry points launched simultaneously produce TWO loops. Or: a stale record after an unclean death makes the guard refuse forever, so the system stays silently dead — the failure mode that is worse than the one the guard prevents.
carries: the staleness threshold (in beats) and the ATOMIC claim. Read-then-act is not atomic; the claim must be. Both are named in the parent's gate_findings as the two missing points.

BUILDME.need: ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness — there is nothing to read until the record exists

the ground loop rebuilt to Akien's 2026-07-30 ruling (scans each device's ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/groundloop/ each beat and posts to the bus on a met trigger). Akien: 'once this is done, the very next intention is...' — this whole family sits downstream of that. decisions/2026-07-30-the-ground-loop-scans-disk-and-posts-to-the-bus.json

watchme: none, because the parent's WATCHME(liveness-read) watches exactly this seam and a second probe on the same object would be two watches of one thing.

relation_to_superclaude_starts_itself.found_at_cast: The ticket superclaude-starts-itself already exists and stands at [PROVEME] — 'the launcher brings up the floor it needs, then tells Claude what it could not fix.' Akien's new intention names superclaude as the entry point, so the two touch.
relation_to_superclaude_starts_itself.not_a_duplicate_and_why: Different whys, so a distinction rather than a collision (ask-the-why-to-distinguish). superclaude-starts-itself makes the TOOLS USABLE — venv, editable install, declared deps, `cairn test` — and its scope was ruled build-minimal by Akien: 'import root + the verb.' This ticket makes the RUNTIME LIVE EXACTLY ONCE. One is about a session being able to work; the other is about a resident process not being started twice.
relation_to_superclaude_starts_itself.who_owns_the_guard: Not superclaude. Akien said 'ONE OF the entry points,' which settles it: a guard living in one caller is re-derived by every future caller (Law 1), so it belongs with the thing it protects (Law 6). superclaude gains a CALL, not a policy.
relation_to_superclaude_starts_itself.sequencing_flag_FOR_AKIEN: superclaude-starts-itself is mid-crossing at PROVEME under an explicit build-minimal scope ruling. Adding a ground-loop start to it NOW would widen a ticket while it is being proved — the quiet scope creep that makes a proof mean less than it says. Proposed: let it reach PROVED on its ruled scope, and land the call as this ticket's own work against the launcher afterward. Akien's call to overrule.
